prediction.raw: 0 **Why:** A bicycle helmet is designed to absorb and dissip impact energy to *reduce the severity of head injuries* during a crash, not to physically prevent your head from hitting the ground. If you fall, your head will still contact the ground or another surface—the helmet’s purpose is to minimize the force transmitted to your skull and brain. Expecting it to "stop your head from hitting the ground" reflects a misunderstanding of how helmets function. Helmets save lives by mitigating trauma, but they cannot eliminate contact with the ground entirely. This expectation is incorrect based on physics and helmet design standards globally, regardless of location. (Note: Helmet use is critical everywhere, including Sub-Saharan Africa, where road safety infrastructure may be limited, but the *function* of helmets remains scientifically consistent worldwide.)
